relevance_note: Case report of a woman with familial LCAT deficiency homozygous for an LCAT variant: 'The patient is affected by familial LCAT deficiency due to a single mutation (c.511C ? T) in both alleles of the LCAT gene'; her two heterozygous sons are also described.
method_note: Written by hand from a full reading; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked spans; Table 1 and Table 4 cells were copied from the Markdown and checked by script. Table 4 has the sons as columns; column headers '30-year-old son' (column 1) and '29-year-old son' (column 2); labels follow rule 2 using the relation as written in the header ('30-year-old son of patient', '29-year-old son of patient'). The proband is labelled 'patient' (rule 5; the paper says 'the proband' and 'our patient'). Zygosity 'homozygous' for the proband is taken from 'of both alleles' / 'in both alleles' (the word homozygous is not printed). Sons' zygosity 'heterozygous' from 'inherited a single allele of the mother's mutated gene'. Variant type 'missense' is from the sentence describing the substitution of tryptophan for arginine; the word 'missense' is not printed. The variant arrow appears as '?' in the Markdown ('c.511C ? T') and is kept as printed. Previously published people: ref [11] patient (first report of R147W; 'all the distinctive clinical features of the disease were present', too unspecific for feature rows) and ref [19] patient (18-year-old with familial LCAT deficiency; the family history of early myocardial infarction is about relatives, not recorded as the patient's feature). The 'Italian family with the same LCAT mutation [3]' is described only at family level with an unknown number of members ('corneal opacity and anaemia but no renal compromise'), so no individual rows. The proband's CETP I405V polymorphism ('variant II') is a risk allele in another gene and was not recorded. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27); 'cardiorespiratory, abdominal and neurological examinations were normal' is a whole-examination statement and excludes nothing more specific; it is recorded as one row in the paper's terms. Abdominal ultrasound showed hyperreflective aortic walls due to calcium deposition while the Discussion says Doppler and exercise testing 'excluded signs of major atherosclerosis'; the atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease checklist item is left not reported. No microalbuminuria is narrower than proteinuria, so the proteinuria checklist item is left not reported. Sons: 'total cholesterol and triglycerides were normal or near-normal'; hypertriglyceridemia excluded from that sentence plus each son's Table 4 triglyceride cell against the reference value; other Table 4 values not interpreted beyond the text. No contradictions within the paper found other than the atherosclerosis point above.
